unprotected sex at least 7 days prior to ovulation. Giving 9 days before 
would leave a decent redundancy to account for any fluctuations. This app 
may predict well the first ovulation but sometimes you may ovulate more 
than once. An egg is at maximum viable for about 24 hours and the app has a 
prediction accuracy of about 2 days so leave 4 days for fertile ovulation 
period . In total that makes 13 days of no sex or sex with protection, this 
is a little under half the length of the average cycle of 28 days.

I love this app and how in tune with my own body it makes me feel. Great for keeping track of your general health, but also protecting yourself from unplanned pregnancy (It puts you more in control as you know how high the risk is on any given day in your cycle).  I was sceptical at first about an apps capabilities to predict "safe" sex days, but actually when you look at how it works and what is taken into account in the algorithms, it is clear why it is certified as so highly effective with proper use. In the tests it beat condoms and almost matched the pill in effectiveness with perfect use. Most of the women who did conceive while testing the app had unprotected sex on a red (unsafe) day, and only 0.5% on a wrongly attributed green (safe) day. BUT I would argue that even using the app, you've still got the option to use condoms or other methods to protect yourself on a red or even a green day, so although you might have your doubts about its efficacy on its own, there are options to increase your safety.   It's also very useful for planning ahead for when your periods will arrive. Much more accurate than normal period tracking apps as it takes into account your temperature, whether or not you are planning to conceive. And if you do decide to try to get pregnant you can switch the app over and use all the data you already collected to help you to plan it!   Arguably a little bit pricey (£50 for the year), however this includes a certified basal thermometer for you to use for your measurements. I would probably carry on using this app as it puts me in touch with my body more and I understand my cycles way better now. Something I think all women can benefit from whether they use contraception or not.

All women deciding to use this app should be aware of all of the science 
involved in conception/contraception. Sperm can survive, still viable, for 
up to 7 days once in the fallopian tubes. All women's cycles vary even 
those with regular cycles have fluctuations. So you need to stop 
unprotected sex at least 7 days prior to ovulation. Giving 9 days before 
would leave a decent redundancy to account for any fluctuations. This app 
may predict well the first ovulation but sometimes you may ovulate more 
than once. An egg is at maximum viable for about 24 hours and the app has a 
prediction accuracy of about 2 days so leave 4 days for fertile ovulation 
period . In total that makes 13 days of no sex or sex with protection, this 
is a little under half the length of the average cycle of 28 days.

I love this app and how in tune with my own body it makes me feel. Even if you aren't planning a pregnancy, or still intend to use protection (as I do even on most green days), it is so valuable to know how long your cycles last and when your ovulation is. Great for keeping track of your general health, but also protecting yourself from unplanned pregnancy (It puts you more in control as you know how high the risk is on any given day in your cycle).  I was sceptical at first about an apps capabilities to predict "safe" sex days, but actually when you look at how it works and what is taken into account in the algorithms, it is clear why it is certified as so highly effective with proper use. In the tests it beat condoms and almost matched the pill in effectiveness with perfect use. Most of the women who did conceive while testing the app had unprotected sex on a red (unsafe) day, and only 0.5% on a wrongly attributed green (safe) day. BUT I would argue that even using the app, you've still got the option to use condoms or other methods to protect yourself on a red or even a green day, so although you might have your doubts about its efficacy on its own, there are options to increase your safety.   It's also very useful for planning ahead for when your periods will arrive. Much more accurate than normal period tracking apps as it takes into account your temperature, whether or not you are planning to conceive. And if you do decide to try to get pregnant you can switch the app over and use all the data you already collected to help you to plan it!   Arguably a little bit pricey (£50 for the year), however this includes a certified basal thermometer for you to use for your measurements. I would probably carry on using this app as it puts me in touch with my body more and I understand my cycles way better now. Something I think all women can benefit from whether they use contraception or not.

Not being able to record that I took the Plan B lead my tracker to believe I might have PCOS and I’m sure had the tracker been able to identify that there was a cause behind my symptoms it’s suggestions would’ve been more accurate. With that being said I enjoy Flo a lot, I even made my partner download it so he can see what’s going on too (that perk is so crafty) I recommend this app to anyone who’s searching for the most convenient and enjoyable period tracker!

This discrepancy has caused me to get multiple stress-inducing alerts about my cycle length and variability being abnormal, when it actually isn’t. 2) There should be more clarity about predicted ovulation dates and “your period is late” warnings. The late period warnings show up based on your averages, not based on actual ovulation dates (which can vary and influence cycle length). Education or disclaimers that accompany “your period is late” notifications about how the timing of your ovulation impacts the length of your cycle could be helpful for reducing stress. I absolutely love this app. I have PCOS and had been TTC for years unsuccessfully. In 2022 I had an early miscarriage and the doctor that I saw told me about the app as she had similar issues. I began using the app to track bbt and LH and got pregnant with my rainbow baby. 

The community on the app is great and there are a ton of great features, but the one thing that prevents me from giving the app 5 stars is that it doesn’t take into account people with abnormal cycles when predicting the ovulation window and next period. 

I understand initially not being able to predict for someone with an abnormal cycle length, but if the person is continuously using the app and tracking LH and their periods, it should after a couple cycles. If you see a pattern in the cycle length the app should be able to start predicting based on the records. For example with help from medication, my cycles are starting to be a little bit more normal as far as predictability goes even though my average cycle is 71 to 72 days which is still abnormal. 

Even though I continuously track, and you can clearly see that my cycle days are up to that point consistently the app still predicts my fertile window to be about five days after the last date of my menstrual cycle and then it tells me I’m in the two week wait. During this time it tells me to keep checking and testing to see if I’m pregnant, which can get annoying, especially because it pops up when you get close to the end of the two week wait it asks when you open up the app in the morning if you took a pregnancy test and if I say no, it’s telling me I should test which I know I shouldn’t because I know I have an ovulated yet. 

I understand the app, not being able to predict if somebody really truly does have irregular cycles where one cycle is 60 days and then the next one is 180 days. In that situation it makes sense that the app wouldn’t be able to predict because there’s no consistency, but the fact that when there is consistency it’s just not fitting into the normal range, the app still can’t manage to do a more accurate prediction is frustrating.

Even with this issue, I still find this app to be better than others. I have tried and as I mentioned, I was able to successfully get pregnant and have my rainbow baby by using this application. I will continue to use this app going forward because it does help and most things about it are fantastic. I hope that this helps anyone who has abnormal cycle length or irregular cycles as well. I also hope that’s the makers and designers a Premom will see this and help fix this issue since there seems to be a large number of individuals with PCOS that use the application.

It got rejected, I pushed back and finally got it taken out of my deductible but no reimbursement. Then they changed to say it should be covered under your Rx insurance. I never tried that but I noticed they’ve now changed it to say HSA/FSA will reimburse you. Maybe they will and maybe they won’t. Again, haven’t tried. At this point I’m not sure I would trust Natural Cycles on their reimbursement promises. 
Final thoughts: if you are pro-life, I would suggest finding a different app. Natural Cycles medical advisory board includes a medical professional who has actively helped develop abortion medication. 2) This is not a passive method and you have to make sure you’re getting as many temperatures as possible, tracking your menstruation, and (though not required but definitely helpful) taking LH tests when the app suggests. 3) You also have to be comfortable enough with your partner to be able to communicate which part of your cycle you’re in and what that means for your method of protection on that day.

This will make it harder for the algorithm to predict your cycle and it will likely be much less accurate than someone who sleeps 8hrs straight. You would need the invest in the tech and subscriptions for the apple watch or aura ring to make it more accurate. 

Waking up throughout the night makes it hard to know when to take your temperature, and unless you want to be checking the clock and counting the hours in your head at 3AM and taking your temp this method will probably drive you crazy like it did for me.

To be clear: this app may work for some, but only if you sleep like a robot. You must take your temperature the instant you wake up, with at least 3-4 hours of uninterrupted sleep beforehand. If you so much as stir or check the time in the early morning, your reading is invalid. This unrealistic rigidity triggered major sleep anxiety for me — I’d wake up early thinking I needed to take my temperature, which made me even more sleep-deprived and less able to get an accurate reading. It created a feedback loop of poor sleep and unreliable results. Eventually, I had to abandon the app altogether and pay monthly for an alternative method that actually works for my body.

I stopped using Natural Cycles after just a few months. My account was inactive for over eight months. Then, I was charged another $120 for a product I haven’t touched since last year— and when I kindly emailed support within hours of the renewal, explaining everything— how their product was useless for me and how I needed the money to pay for other contraception, they flatly denied my refund request because I didn’t cancel “24 hours before.” No grace period. No human understanding. No flexibility.

I understand policies exist. But ethical businesses don’t hide behind them when it’s clear a customer isn’t trying to game the system and is just asking for fairness.

Natural Cycles may work for a small subset of people, but it’s built on incredibly rigid input requirements that are incompatible with many women’s real lives. And if it doesn’t work for you, don’t expect a shred of empathy or basic decency from their customer service.

Think twice before trusting this app with your health — or your wallet.

Tracking periods can help people understand their bodies, know when to expect their cycle, and prepare with the right products. It would be great if the app supported everyone who needs it.

It provides so much great info & knowledge to the primary user, whilst giving a very top line & often quite cringe sentence on the current phase of the cycle to the partner. The app provides an additional short paragraph on each subcategory (mind, body, diet) but with very little reasoning behind their recommendations.

It would be great to see a much more granular, detailed, scientific daily description of each phase. The roles & potential effects of changes of individual hormones. Visibility of symptoms primary user has input on that specific (if they choose to share). 

The reactions & secret requests functions are fun, but don’t really get to the core of being aware, mindful & supportive to the primary user. 

I understand this interface is not a priority for the app, but with extra info it could be great - currently it makes more sense for me to just sign in as the primary user for full visibility (as we have done with other apps in the market), certainly NOT worth the subscription as a partner at this stage.
